import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by finitely many generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and
finitely many relators. Its word problem is the set of words over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ that represent the identity element. By the
McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem, finitely presented residually finite groups have decidable
(recursive) word problem; the question is whether the word problem can fail to be
primitive recursive. Whether the word problem is (primitive) recursive does not depend on
the chosen finite presentation, so the formalisation quantifies over finite presentations.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if every non-identity element $g \in G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in some finite quotient
of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- The word problem of the group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$
presented by `rels`: the predicate on words `w` over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ (encoded as lists of pairs `(i, b)`, where `b = true`
stands for $x_i$ and `b = false` for $x_i^{-1}$) that holds when `w` represents the identity
element of the presented group. -/
def WordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (w : List (Fin n × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- The empty word represents the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_nil {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : WordProblem rels [] :=
  map_one _

/--
Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

That is, is there a finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$
(with $\mathrm{rels}$ finite) of a residually finite group whose word problem, as a predicate on
words over $x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$, is decidable (`ComputablePred`) but is not
decidable by a primitive recursive function (`PrimrecPred`)? Primitive recursiveness is taken
with respect to the standard `Primcodable` encoding of words as elements of `List (Fin n × Bool)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.15» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ComputablePred (WordProblem rels) ∧ ¬ PrimrecPred (WordProblem rels) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.15»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; the notes' guidance (quantify over a finite presentation, phrase primitive recursiveness of the word-problem set using Mathlib's Primrec/ComputablePred machinery) was followed.
modeling_decisions: The statement quantifies over finite presentations (n generators, finite relator set) rather than over abstract groups with an IsFinitelyPresented predicate; since the (primitive) recursiveness of the word problem is invariant under change of finite presentation, this is equivalent to the informal existence question (as the decomposition notes allow).

'Recursive solution of the word problem' is rendered as Mathlib's ComputablePred (decidable set of words); 'primitive recursive' as Mathlib's PrimrecPred. Both are relative to the standard Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool) (Primcodable.list over Primcodable.prod/fin/bool); primitive recursive predicates are closed under primitive-recursive re-encodings, so the choice of standard encoding does not affect the statement.
The redundant hypothesis ComputablePred (automatic by McKinsey–Mal'cev for f.p. residually finite groups) is kept because the source statement explicitly includes 'recursive'.
Residual finiteness is defined via finite-index normal subgroups (equivalently, separation by homomorphisms to finite groups) to avoid universe quantification over finite groups.
Two short @[category test] lemmas (finite groups are residually finite; the empty word is in the word problem) were added as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md.
AMS tags 3 (logic/computability) and 20 (group theory).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by a finite presentation
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$. Its word problem is the set of
words over the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ that represent the identity. Whether this set is
recursive, or primitive recursive, does not depend on the chosen finite presentation,
so the statement fixes one. By the McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem the word problem of a
finitely presented residually finite group is always recursive, so the question is
whether it can fail to be primitive recursive.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if every non-identity element $g$ lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index. Equivalently, for every $g \neq 1$ there is a
homomorphism from $G$ to a finite group that does not kill $g$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- Finite groups are residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- The word problem of the presentation $\langle \alpha \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$: a word
$w$ over the letters $x^{\pm 1}$, $x \in \alpha$ (encoded as a list of pairs
`(x, b)`, where `b = true` stands for $x$ and `b = false` for $x^{-1}$), belongs to the
word problem if and only if it represents the identity of the presented group. -/
def wordProblem {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) (w : List (α × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A word lies in the word problem if and only if the free group element it spells
lies in the normal closure of the relators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_iff {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) (w : List (α × Bool)) :
    wordProblem rels w ↔ FreeGroup.mk w ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure rels :=
  PresentedGroup.mk_eq_one_iff

/-- For the presentation with no relators, a word is in the word problem if and only if it
spells the identity of the free group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_empty {α : Type*} (w : List (α × Bool)) :
    wordProblem (∅ : Set (FreeGroup α)) w ↔ FreeGroup.mk w = 1 := by
  rw [wordProblem_iff, le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp)),
    Subgroup.mem_bot]

/--
Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

That is, is there a finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$
of a residually finite group whose word problem (the set of words over $x_i^{\pm 1}$
representing the identity) is a recursive set but not a primitive recursive set?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.15» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ComputablePred (wordProblem rels) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred (wordProblem rels) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.15»

Every finitely presented group is isomorphic to such a group, and residual finiteness as well as recursiveness/primitive recursiveness of the word problem are independent of the chosen finite presentation (translation between finite presentations is a primitive recursive substitution), so fixing the presentation is without loss of generality, as the decomposition notes suggest.

'Recursive' is formalized as Mathlib's ComputablePred and 'primitive recursive' as Mathlib's PrimrecPred, both relative to Mathlib's Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool). This encoding is primitive-recursively interconvertible with standard Gödel encodings of words, so the notions agree with the classical ones.

The (redundant, by McKinsey–Mal'cev) condition 'recursive solution of the word problem' is kept explicitly as ComputablePred to mirror the statement's wording; it does not change the mathematical content.

Residual finiteness is defined via finite-index normal subgroups rather than homomorphisms to finite groups; the two are classically equivalent and the former avoids quantifying over a universe of finite groups.

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element remains
nonidentity under some homomorphism to a finite group. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q), f g ≠ 1

/--
Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but
not primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

Here `n` and `rels` give a finite presentation on the generators `Fin n`. Its
word problem is the predicate on signed words `List (Fin n × Bool)` saying that
their image in the presented group is the identity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.15» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsResiduallyFinite
          (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ComputablePred (fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1) ∧
      ¬PrimrecPred (fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.15»

The word problem is stated on raw signed words `List (Fin n × Bool)` via `FreeGroup.mk` followed by `PresentedGroup.mk`; this uses Mathlib's canonical `Primcodable` instance for that finite-alphabet word type.
Recursive decidability is expressed by `ComputablePred`, and failure of every primitive-recursive decision procedure by `¬ PrimrecPred`, for the same word-problem predicate.
Residual finiteness is modeled by requiring every nonidentity element to have nonidentity image under a homomorphism to some finite group.

The theorem fixes an existentially chosen finite presentation; primitive-recursive decidability of a finitely generated group's word problem is presentation-independent, so this faithfully captures the existence question.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

By the McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem, every finitely presented residually finite group has
a recursive (decidable) word problem. The question is whether the word problem of
such a group can fail to be primitive recursive.

The word problem of a group $G$ with respect to a finite generating tuple
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ is the set of words over the alphabet
$\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}\}$ that represent the identity of $G$. For a finitely
generated group, whether this set is recursive, resp. primitive recursive, does not depend
on the choice of the finite generating tuple: a change of generators is a fixed
substitution of words, which is primitive recursive.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
and finitely many relations. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ in $G$ there is a normal
subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$, i.e. every non-identity element
survives in some finite quotient of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- The *word problem* of a group $G$ with respect to a tuple $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of elements
of $G$: the set of words $w$ over the alphabet $\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}\}$ that
represent the identity of $G$.

A word is a list of letters `(i, b) : Fin n × Bool`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and
`(i, false)` for $x_i^{-1}$, as in `FreeGroup.mk`. -/
def wordProblem {G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → G) : Set (List (Fin n × Bool)) :=
  {w | FreeGroup.lift x (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1}

/--
Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

That is, is there a finitely presented residually finite group $G$ with a finite generating
tuple $x_1, \dots, x_n$ such that the set of words over $\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}\}$
representing the identity of $G$ is recursive (decidable) but not primitive recursive?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.15» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → G), Subgroup.closure (Set.range x) = ⊤ ∧
        ComputablePred (· ∈ wordProblem x) ∧ ¬ PrimrecPred (· ∈ wordProblem x) := by
  sorry

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relations is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Finite groups are residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- The empty word represents the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem nil_mem_wordProblem {G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → G) :
    [] ∈ wordProblem x := by
  simp [wordProblem]

end Kourovka.«5.15»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot yes/no existence reading is correct and the notes' guidance (quantify over a finite presentation/generating set, phrase primitive recursiveness of the word-problem set via Mathlib's PrimrecPred rather than of the group) was followed.
modeling_decisions: The group is quantified as an abstract `G : Type` that is finitely presented (isomorphic to some PresentedGroup with finitely many generators and relators) rather than fixing G := PresentedGroup rels. Both are equivalent; the abstract form mirrors the wording 'there exist ... groups'.

The word problem is taken with respect to an existentially chosen finite generating tuple x : Fin n → G (with Subgroup.closure (Set.range x) = ⊤). For a finitely generated group, recursiveness and primitive recursiveness of the word problem are independent of the finite generating tuple (a change of generators is a fixed word substitution, which is primitive recursive), so ∃ over generating tuples is equivalent to ∀; the generating condition is essential to exclude spurious witnesses from non-generating tuples.

'Recursive solution of the word problem' is formalized as ComputablePred (· ∈ wordProblem x) and 'not primitive recursive' as ¬ PrimrecPred (· ∈ wordProblem x), using Mathlib's encodings of List (Fin n × Bool) via the Primcodable instances. Both predicates existentially quantify their DecidablePred, so no classical decidability instance is needed. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

The word problem of a group $G$ given by a finite presentation
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ is the set of words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$ that represent the identity of $G$. By the McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem, every
finitely presented residually finite group has a recursive (decidable) word problem. The
question asks whether this solution can nevertheless fail to be primitive recursive.

Whether the word problem of a finitely presented group is recursive, or primitive recursive,
does not depend on the chosen finite presentation: a change of finite presentation induces a
primitive recursive substitution on words. Hence it is no loss of generality to quantify over
finite presentations, with generators indexed by `Fin n` and a finite set of relators.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/--
A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element $g \in G$ lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in some finite quotient of $G$.
-/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- Every subgroup of a residually finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsResiduallyFinite G)
    (H : Subgroup G) : IsResiduallyFinite H := by
  intro g hg
  obtain ⟨N, hN, hNfin, hgN⟩ := h g (by simpa using hg)
  exact ⟨N.subgroupOf H, hN.subgroupOf H, inferInstance, hgN⟩

/--
The *word problem* of the group presented by generators `α` and relators `rels`: the
predicate on words `w : List (α × Bool)` (formal products of the letters $x_a^{\pm 1}$,
where `(a, true)` stands for $x_a$ and `(a, false)` for $x_a^{-1}$) that holds precisely when
`w` represents the identity of `PresentedGroup rels`.
-/
def wordProblem {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) (w : List (α × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A word represents the identity of the presented group if and only if the corresponding
element of the free group lies in the normal closure of the relators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_iff_mem_normalClosure {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α))
    (w : List (α × Bool)) :
    wordProblem rels w ↔ FreeGroup.mk w ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure rels :=
  PresentedGroup.mk_eq_one_iff

/-- The empty word represents the identity of any presented group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_nil {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) : wordProblem rels [] := by
  simp [wordProblem, ← FreeGroup.one_eq_mk]

/-- Every relator, read as a word, represents the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_of_mem {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) (w : List (α × Bool))
    (hw : FreeGroup.mk w ∈ rels) : wordProblem rels w :=
  PresentedGroup.one_of_mem hw

/-- The word problem of a free group (no relators) asks whether a word freely reduces to the
empty word. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_empty {α : Type*} (w : List (α × Bool)) :
    wordProblem (∅ : Set (FreeGroup α)) w ↔ FreeGroup.mk w = 1 := by
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure (∅ : Set (FreeGroup α)) = ⊥ :=
    le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _))
  simp [wordProblem_iff_mem_normalClosure, this]

/--
**McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem.** A finitely presented residually finite group has recursive
(decidable) word problem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 20]
theorem computablePred_wordProblem_of_isResiduallyFinite (n : ℕ)
    (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
    (h : IsResiduallyFinite (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))) :
    ComputablePred (wordProblem (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) := by
  sorry

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

That is, is there a finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$
of a residually finite group such that the set of words in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ that
represent the identity is recursive (decidable) but not primitive recursive?
-/

    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsResiduallyFinite (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ComputablePred (wordProblem (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred (wordProblem (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.15»
